examples.name: gauge_support_pair
examples.primal: k = gamma_C for a closed convex set C containing 0
examples.teaching_point: The polar gauge is the support function of the primal unit set.

examples.name: indicator_pair
examples.teaching_point: The extended polar sends feasible-set membership to membership in the polar set.

examples.name: linf_l1_norms
examples.teaching_point: The square unit ball and diamond polar give the max/sum dual pair.

examples.name: lp_lq_norms
examples.teaching_point: Holder's inequality is the polar gauge inequality.

examples.name: quadratic_norm
examples.primal: k(x) = sqrt(x^T Q x), Q positive definite
examples.teaching_point: Polar ellipsoids invert the shape matrix.

examples.name: degree_p_function
examples.teaching_point: Gauge polarity feeds the Fenchel conjugate of homogeneous convex powers.
